(Omaha, Nebraska) | college = *[[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] (2021–2023) *[[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]] (2023–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|start}} | team1 = [[Philadelphia 76ers]] | years2 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]] | team2 = →[[Delaware Blue Coats]] | years3 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team3 = [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]] | highlights = * 2× First-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2024, 2025) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2021]]) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2021) }} '''Hunter Amon Sallis''' (born March 26, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]] and [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]]. ==High school career== Sallis did not start on his middle school basketball team but earned a spot on the [[varsity team]] as a freshman at [[Millard North High School]] in [[Omaha, Nebraska]].{{cite web |last=Grace |first=Erin |title=As Hunter Sallis learns to fly, the Millard North star is on an upward trajectory in the hoops world |url=https://omaha.com/sports/high-school/as-hunter-sallis-learns-to-fly-the-millard-north-star-is-on-an-upward-trajectory/article_94ce2dea-9338-5963-9441-2a2ca4067d03.html |website=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |access-date=April 2, 2021 |date=March 8, 2020}} He was nicknamed "[[Bambi (character)|Bambi]]" due to his lack of coordination at the time.{{cite web |last=Bennett |first=Brian |title=Recruiting notebook: The offers are pouring in for late bloomer Hunter Sallis |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2027020/2020/08/28/recruiting-hunter-sallis-contenders-2021-prospect/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=April 2, 2021 |date=August 28, 2020}} As a senior, Sallis averaged 22.2 points, 4.6 rebounds and 3.8 assists per game, leading Millard North to its first Class A state title in 2021.{{cite web |last=Roberts |first=Ben |title=Five-star point guard Hunter Sallis picks Gonzaga. So what's next for Kentucky? |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-recruiting/article250228305.html |website=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |access-date=April 9, 2021 |date=March 26, 2021}}{{cite web |last=Powell |first=Ron |title=Class A boys: 'We've had redemption on our minds ever since' — Sallis, Johnson lead Millard North to first state title |url=https://journalstar.com/sports/high-school/basketball/boys/class-a-boys-we-ve-had-redemption-on-our-minds-ever-since-sallis-johnson-lead/article_3bf78b23-59fd-5f20-9840-18e442ddf221.html |website=[[Lincoln Journal Star]] |access-date=April 9, 2021 |date=March 13, 2021}} He finished with 1,819 career points, the third-most in Class A history, behind only [[Andre Woolridge]] and [[Erick Strickland]].{{cite web |last=Pospisil |first=Stu |title=Meet the 2021 All-Nebraska boys basketball team |url=https://omaha.com/sports/high-school/meet-the-2021-all-nebraska-boys-basketball-team/article_67259212-93d0-11eb-8237-7b8459984e40.html |website=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |access-date=April 9, 2021 |date=April 4, 2021}} He was named to the rosters for the [[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]].{{cite web |last=Kendeigh |first=Andy |title=Hunter Sallis named McDonald's High School All-American |url=https://www.ketv.com/article/hunter-sallis-named-mcdonald-s-high-school-all-american/35607556 |website=[[KETV]] |access-date=April 9, 2021 |date=February 23, 2021}} Additionally, he was named the Nebraska [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]].{{cite web |title=Hunter Sallis 2020 - 2021 Boys Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/hunter-sallis/38361 |access-date=April 23, 2023 |website=playeroftheyear.gatorade.com}} ===Recruiting=== Sallis was rated a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[ESPN]] and [[247Sports]], and a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. He was the first five-star basketball recruit in Nebraska history.{{cite web |last=Paniagua |first=Hunter |title=Millard North's Hunter Sallis a semifinalist for national player of the year |url=https://omaha.com/sports/high-school/millard-norths-hunter-sallis-a-semifinalist-for-national-player-of-the-year/article_b55be5c6-6711-11eb-b235-e7aa147cde58.html |website=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |access-date=April 9, 2021 |date=February 4, 2021}} On March 26, 2021, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] over offers from [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] and [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]].{{cite web |last=Meehan |first=Jim |title=5-star guard Hunter Sallis commits to Gonzaga, becomes highest-rated recruit in program history |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2021/mar/26/standout-guard-hunter-sallis-commits-to-gonzaga/ |website=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |access-date=April 9, 2021 |date=March 26, 2021}} He became the highest-ranked recruit in program history until [[Chet Holmgren]] committed a month later.{{cite web |title=Hunter Sallis, 5-star guard, becomes highest-ranked recruit in Gonzaga history |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4220193/2021/03/26/hunter-sallis-5-star-guard-becomes-highest-ranked-recruit-in-gonzaga-history/ |website=[[The |date=April 7, 2023}} As a sophomore, Sallis averaged 4.5 points, 2.2 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://gozags.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/hunter-sallis/4281|title=Hunter Forest]].{{cite news |title=Former Gonzaga guard Hunter Sallis transfers to Wake Forest: How he fits with the program |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4454488/2023/04/26/hunter-sallis-transfer-wake-forest/ |access-date=January 26, 2024 |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=April 26, 2023}} On November 29, 2023, Sallis scored 24 points and 4 assists in a 82-71 win against [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401574554|title=Sallis scores 24 points, Carr 22 and Wake Forest pulls away late to top Florida in ACC/SEC Challenge|date=November 29, 2023|website=[[ESPN.com]]|access-date=March 7, 2024}} On December 30, 2023, Sallis web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401604098|title=Sallis scores 20, leads Wake Forest over Virginia Tech 86-63|date=December 30, 2023|website=[[ESPN.com]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=March 7, 2024}} On January 2, 2024, Sallis scored 21 points and 3 assists in a 84-78 win over [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|NC State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.bloggersodear.com/2024/2/10/24068809/wake-forest-grits-out-revenge-win-over-nc-state|title=Wake Forest grits out revenge win over NC State|last=Thayer|first=Essex|date=February 10, 2024|website=Blogger So Dear|access-date=March 7, 2024}} On February 24, 2024, Sallis scored 29 points and 6 rebounds in a 83-79 win over [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401604210|title=Wake Forest edges No.8 Duke 83-79, Court storming leaves Filipowski shaken up|date=February 24, 2024|website=[[ESPN.com]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=March 7, 2024}} On February 26, 2024, Sallis earned [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) player of the week honors after averaging 23.0 points, 5.0 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2024/2/26/wfs-sallis-nds-burton-claim-acc-mens-basketball-weekly-honors.aspx|title=WF's Sallis, ND's Burton Claim ACC Men's Basketball Weekly Honors|date=February 26, 2024|publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|access-date=March 7, 2024}} ==Professional career== On June 26, 2025 after being undrafted in the [[2025 NBA draft]], Sallis signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsportsphiladelphia.com/nba/philadelphia-76ers/report-sixers-to-sign-hunter-sallis-2-way-contract-nba-undrafted-free-agents/672639/|title=Sixers to sign Hunter Sallis to 2-way contract|date=June 26, 2025|publisher=[[NBC Sports Philadelphia]]|access-date=June 29, 2025}} He made seven appearances for the 76ers, averaging 1.0 point, 0.1 rebounds, and 0.6 assists. On December 24, Sallis was waived by Philadelphia following the signing of [[MarJon Beauchamp]].{{Cite web|title=76ers sign former 1st-round pick from Bucks to new contract|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/76ers-sign-former-1st-round-151743237.html|access-date=December 24, 2025}} He was then signed by the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego
